scopeNote: V2 econ/intent scan. V1 (src/Phlimbo.sol) read for diff reference only and is OUT of scope. Linear-depletion exponential-decay under-delivery (V1 ledger M-04) is EXCLUDED by mandate — V2 removed the _updatePool rate recompute that caused it; verified absent at PhlimboV2.sol L465-467.
lawHierarchy: 1) No exploits (recall>tidiness). 2) Faithfulness to story-020/021. 3) Owner/migrator/hook trusted for KNOWING actions; non-obvious footguns + third-party-mountable attacks IN scope.

findings.title: Strict balance equality (==) in settleDebt/migrateDeposits lets ANY third party brick the one-shot migration with a 1-wei token donation
findings.description: settleDebt requires `usdc.balanceOf(this) == totalUSDC` (L159) AND `phUSD.balanceOf(this) == totalPHUSD_deposited` (L161); migrateDeposits requires the same strict phUSD equality (L207-210). USDC and phUSD are freely transferable ERC20s, so any external address can transfer 1 wei of either token to the migrator address and push `balanceOf` to `total + 1`, making every subsequent settleDebt/migrateDeposits call revert on the precondition. The migration is a one-shot, owner-driven lifecycle; the only recovery is `withdrawAll()` (which drains the entire legit float to the owner) followed by an exact re-fund of the current public `totalUSDC`/`totalPHUSD_deposited` figures — after which the attacker can immediately re-donate 1 wei and brick it again.
findings.economicImpact: Indefinite, repeatable denial-of-service on the entire V1->V2 migration at a cost of 1 wei + gas per round. User funds are not stolen (recovery exists and accounting stays internally consistent — settleDebt mints phUSD to users without touching the migrator's phUSD balance, and migrateDeposits decrements balance and totalPHUSD_deposited in lockstep), but every settle/migrate batch can be stalled, forcing an owner withdrawAll+refund cycle per griefing round and stranding migrating users in limbo.
findings.attackOrFootgun: attack (third-party-mountable) + owner over-funding footgun. Attack: 1) owner funds migrator exactly. 2) attacker transfers 1 wei phUSD (or USDC) to migrator. 3) settleDebt/migrateDeposits revert with 'phUSD balance mismatch'/'USDC balance mismatch'. 4) owner withdrawAll + re-fund. 5) attacker re-donates -> repeat. Footgun variant: owner over-funds by any amount (or funds before knowing the exact public total after a partial settle) -> same brick, same withdrawAll+refund recovery.
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 — third-party-mountable availability attack on a live migration; recall over tidiness. The donation/over-funding griefing is NOT a malicious-owner vector, so it is in scope; the strict-== was a deliberate 'catch over-funding mistakes' design (per L153-154 comment) whose non-obvious consequence (anyone-can-brick) makes it a Law-3 footgun as well.
findings.remediationHint: Use `>=` with the surplus swept/ignored, or check exact required amount with a tolerance and sweep dust, rather than strict `==`.

findings.title: Migrator-routed auto-claim sends a pre-existing V2 staker's pending rewards to the migrator, not the user
findings.description: During migrateDeposits, MigratorV1V2 calls `phlimboV2.stake(dep, user)` with msg.sender = migrator. stake() L336-338 auto-claims any pending rewards for an existing position via `_claimRewards(user, msg.sender)`, routing the reward beneficiary to msg.sender (the migrator), not the user (L486-501, L495/L500). If a user already holds a V2 position when the migrator stakes their V1 deposit on top — realistic because V2 is deployed and permissionlessly stakeable during the migration window, so an eager user can self-stake first — the phUSD + stable rewards accrued on that self-stake are minted/transferred to the MIGRATOR. The migrator has no logic to forward these (settleDebt pays only the seeded snapshot amounts), so they sit in the migrator and are ultimately swept to the owner via withdrawAll.
findings.economicImpact: Silent leakage of a self-migrating user's accrued V2 rewards (phUSD + stable) to the migrator/owner. Magnitude is bounded by the rewards accrued on the user's self-staked amount over the migration window — typically small for a short window, but permanent and unrecoverable by the user.
findings.attackOrFootgun: footgun / value-leak (not attacker-profitable; the loser is the eager self-staking user). Trigger: user self-stakes into live V2 -> accrues rewards -> migrator later runs migrateDeposits and stakes their V1 deposit -> user's pending V2 rewards auto-claim to the migrator.
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 (value leak from a user) + Law 3 (the 'rewards land in caller, not user' routing during delegation is a subtle, non-obvious consequence of the V2 migrator design). Not a malicious-owner vector.
findings.remediationHint: During migrator-delegated stake, route auto-claim to `user` rather than `msg.sender`, or document/operationally prevent users from self-staking V2 before migration completes.

findings.title: pause -> pauseWithdraw -> unpause OVER-MINTS phUSD: stale phUSDPerSecond (sized for pre-pause stake) accrues over the shrunken stake
findings.description: pauseWithdraw (L280-291) decrements `user.amount` and `totalStaked` but does NOT call `_updatePhUSDEmissionRate`, so `phUSDPerSecond` remains sized for the larger pre-pause `totalStaked` (S0). On unpause, the next `_updatePool` accrues `timeElapsed * phUSDPerSecond` (L472) divided by the shrunken `totalStaked` (S1) into `accPhUSDPerShare` (L473), inflating per-share phUSD accrual by a factor of S0/S1 until the rate is refreshed by the next stake/withdraw/setDesiredAPY. Verified: overMintFactor = S0/S1, matching V1. Carries verbatim from V1 (pauseWithdraw + the emission-rate-omission are byte-identical to V1).
findings.economicImpact: Survivors over-mint phUSD by ~(S0/S1 - 1) on the phUSD reward accrued during the [unpause, next rate refresh] interval. Severity is APY-gated: with desiredAPYBps == 0 (current/likely config) phUSDPerSecond == 0 and there is NO over-mint (immunized — confirmed at L471). RE-ASSESS TO MEDIUM/HIGH if any non-zero-APY config ships; the over-mint then inflates phUSD supply against backing.
findings.attackOrFootgun: footgun amplified by pause operations; the over-mint is automatic, no attacker needed. A staker who happens to remain after others pauseWithdraw passively over-mints.
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 (uncollateralized phUSD over-mint) conditional on non-zero APY. Pause is pauser-driven; the stale-rate consequence is non-obvious -> Law 3 footgun.
findings.remediationHint: Call `_updatePool()` then `_updatePhUSDEmissionRate()` inside pauseWithdraw, or recompute the rate on unpause.

findings.title: phUSD mint authority is load-bearing for solvency: revocation/pause/cap bricks claim/stake/withdraw (and now settleDebt) with no graceful degradation
findings.description: _claimRewards (L495) calls `phUSD.mint(beneficiary, pendingPhUSDAmount)`. Because stake (L337), withdraw (L373), and claim (L424) all funnel through _claimRewards, revoking/pausing/capping the migrator-or-pool's phUSD mint privilege (IFlax.revokeAllMintPrivileges / authorizedMinters / supply cap) makes every reward-bearing interaction revert, with no path to claim accrued phUSD or to withdraw without first claiming. Only pauseWithdraw (L280-291, no mint) preserves a principal-only exit, and only while paused. Carries from V1. AMPLIFIED in the V2 system: MigratorV1V2.settleDebt also mints phUSD (L181), so a mint-right revocation mid-migration additionally bricks settlement of V1 reward obligations.
findings.economicImpact: Protocol availability failure: stakers cannot claim accrued phUSD rewards and cannot withdraw principal through the normal path while mint is unavailable. The pre-V2 phUSD already accrued is effectively frozen until mint is restored. During migration, settleDebt halts, stranding V1 reward obligations.
findings.attackOrFootgun: footgun (owner/phUSD-token-owner KNOWING action of revoking mint has a non-obvious consequence of bricking withdraw, not just rewards). Per IFlax, mintVersion/revokeAllMintPrivileges are owner tools whose blast radius on the staking pool is non-obvious.
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 (loss of access to funds) + Law 3 (non-obvious footgun of mint-right management). Not a malicious-owner framing.
findings.remediationHint: Decouple principal withdrawal from reward minting (allow withdraw to skip/queue phUSD mint on failure), and sequence migration so mint right is not revoked before settleDebt completes.

findings.title: _claimRewards underflows and reverts after pauseWithdraw -> unpause -> claim (stale phUSDDebt/stableDebt on shrunken amount)
findings.inheritedFrom: phlimbo-ea ledger M-01 (V1, downgraded to Low)
findings.description: pauseWithdraw reduces `user.amount` (L285) without updating `user.phUSDDebt`/`user.stableDebt`. On a later claim/withdraw, `_claimRewards` computes `pending = (user.amount * acc) / PRECISION - user.<debt>` (L493/L498); the debt was sized for the pre-pauseWithdraw (larger) amount, so the subtraction can underflow and revert (Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic). Same shape as V1 ledger M-01; pauseWithdraw is unchanged in V2. Now also reachable by migrated positions (migrator sets phUSDDebt on stake, then a pause cycle can strand them).
findings.economicImpact: Self-inflicted, multi-gated reward-claim/withdraw revert for a user who used the emergency pauseWithdraw partially. Principal remains recoverable via re-pause + further pauseWithdraw, so impact is reduced to a temporary claim/withdraw brick — consistent with the V1 Low reclass.
findings.attackOrFootgun: footgun (self-inflicted; requires the user to call pauseWithdraw partially during a pause).
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 (temporary loss of access), Low per the established V1 reclass (self-inflicted, multi-gated, principal recoverable).
findings.remediationHint: Recompute user reward debt inside pauseWithdraw.

findings.title: Stable-reward stranding via per-share rounding: rewardBalance debited in full while accStablePerShare floors
findings.description: _updatePool credits `accStablePerShare += (toDistribute * PRECISION) / totalStaked` (L460, floors) while debiting `rewardBalance -= toDistribute` in full (L463). The floored remainder `(toDistribute * PRECISION) mod totalStaked` is removed from rewardBalance but never credited to any share, so it is permanently uncreditable to stakers and stranded in the contract. Carries verbatim from V1 (the V1 rate-recompute that was removed does not affect this rounding).
findings.economicImpact: Slow, permanent stranding of stable-reward dust proportional to update frequency and totalStaked magnitude; recoverable only via owner emergencyTransfer. Low.
findings.attackOrFootgun: neither (precision-loss design artifact); marginally worsened by frequent pokes (more update events -> more floor remainders), but the new V2 _updatePool no longer re-anchors so the poke incentive is gone.
findings.remediationHint: Carry the rounding remainder forward into the next distribution instead of discarding it.

findings.title: phUSD is BOTH the staking token and a minted reward -> self-referential mint/stake inflation spiral
findings.description: Stakers deposit phUSD (totalStaked) and are rewarded in newly-minted phUSD (_claimRewards L495). phUSDPerSecond scales with totalStaked (L518), so minted phUSD reward can be re-staked to grow totalStaked, which grows the emission rate, which mints more phUSD — a compounding, self-referential inflation loop with no external backing on the phUSD reward leg. Carries from V1.
findings.economicImpact: Tokenomic dilution of phUSD over time; not an exploit but a design-level inflation pressure that compounds with the M-05/over-mint and uncapped-APY items. Low.
findings.attackOrFootgun: neither (tokenomic design); amplifies ECON-003 and ECON-008.
findings.lawBasis: Law 2 (mechanism design vs intended phUSD backing) / Law 1 supply pressure, Low.
findings.remediationHint: Bound phUSD emission against backing, or cap cumulative phUSD minted by the pool.

findings.title: desiredAPYBps is uncapped: two-step gate is delay-only, not magnitude-capped, so phUSD mint pressure is unbounded
findings.description: setDesiredAPY accepts an arbitrary `bps` with no upper bound (L172-190). phUSDPerSecond = totalStaked * desiredAPYBps / 1e4 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR (L518), so a large bps yields proportionally large uncollateralized phUSD emission. The two-step (100-block) preview/commit gate enforces only a delay, not a magnitude cap. Carries from V1.
findings.economicImpact: Owner can set an arbitrarily high APY, minting unbounded phUSD against no backing. Combined with ECON-003 (stale-rate over-mint) and ECON-007 (re-stake spiral), the inflation surface compounds.
findings.attackOrFootgun: centralization / footgun. Setting a typo'd or excessive APY has a non-obvious magnitude consequence (uncapped mint) -> footgun beyond pure centralization.
findings.lawBasis: Law 3 — owner is trusted for KNOWING actions, but an uncapped parameter whose blast radius is unbounded phUSD mint is a non-obvious footgun; surfaced as centralization with safe-config guidance.
findings.remediationHint: Add a sane MAX_APY_BPS bound in setDesiredAPY.

findings.title: setDepletionDuration has no minimum floor: duration=1 turns the next _updatePool into a flash-distribution of the entire rewardBalance to whoever is staked
findings.description: setDepletionDuration has only `_duration > 0` (L197), no minimum floor and no two-step gate. Setting `_duration = 1` makes `rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance * PRECISION / 1` (L208). The next `_updatePool` then computes `potentialReward = rewardPerSecond * timeElapsed / PRECISION = rewardBalance * timeElapsed >= rewardBalance`, which is capped at `rewardBalance` (L457), so the ENTIRE undistributed rewardBalance is credited to `accStablePerShare` over `totalStaked` in a single update — a flash distribution to whoever is staked at that instant. Carries from V1. Re-assessed vs V1: the L457 cap bounds the payout to rewardBalance (not beyond it), so this mis-times the whole stream rather than over-distributing.
findings.economicImpact: The full pending stable reward stream collapses onto current stakers in one block, defeating the linear-depletion intent (story-020/021) and enabling a stake-large-then-shrink-duration MEV capture. Bounded by rewardBalance — no over-distribution, but severe mis-timing/front-running surface.
findings.attackOrFootgun: centralization / footgun. duration=1 is a non-obvious lever; an owner could shrink the window for a legit reason and unknowingly flash-distribute to whoever front-ran in.
findings.lawBasis: Law 2 (violates linear-depletion intent) + Law 3 (non-obvious owner footgun). Not a malicious-owner framing.
findings.remediationHint: Enforce a minimum depletionDuration floor and/or gate duration shrinks behind the two-step delay.

findings.title: Optional hook fires inside withdraw AFTER principal transfer: a reverting/gas-heavy hook bricks stake/withdraw/claim (DoS)
findings.description: The new IPhlimboHook is invoked after state mutation and token transfer in stake (L353-355), withdraw (L398-400), and claim (L429-431), inside the nonReentrant guard. A hook that reverts (or exceeds gas) reverts the entire outer call. For withdraw, onWithdraw fires AFTER the principal safeTransfer (L392) and the _claimRewards transfers, so a reverting hook unwinds an otherwise-complete withdraw, blocking the normal exit path for ALL users until the owner clears the hook via setHook(0). pauseWithdraw (L280-291) deliberately invokes no hook (L278), preserving an emergency principal-only exit while paused.
findings.economicImpact: Pool-wide DoS of stake/withdraw/claim if a buggy/reverting hook is wired. Not fund loss (escape via setHook(0) or pauseWithdraw under pause), but availability failure for all users.
findings.attackOrFootgun: footgun (owner KNOWINGLY sets a hook, but a hook that reverts under some state / runs out of gas is a non-obvious consequence). The interface doc already states the owner is trusted to set non-malicious hooks and that a reverting hook reverts the call — so this is a documented hazard; surfaced as a Low operational footgun for completeness.
findings.lawBasis: Law 3 — owner-set hook with a non-obvious DoS consequence; documented but worth flagging as an operational hazard. Not a malicious-owner finding.
findings.remediationHint: Consider try/catch around hook calls (swallow hook reverts) or gas-limiting the hook invocation so a faulty hook cannot brick core flows.

findings.title: phUSDPerSecond truncates to 0 at low totalStaked x low APY (integer floor)
findings.description: phUSDPerSecond = (totalStaked * desiredAPYBps) / 10000 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR (L518) floors to 0 whenever totalStaked * desiredAPYBps < 1e4 * 31_536_000 (~3.15e11). At the MINIMUM_STAKE (1e15) this only bites for APY below ~3 bps-equivalents of the threshold (i.e. effectively never for sane APY at >= min stake); it bites only at sub-min dust totals combined with tiny APY. Carries from V1 (Low edge).
findings.economicImpact: phUSD rewards silently stop accruing for very small pools / tiny APY. Edge-case under-delivery, Low.
findings.attackOrFootgun: neither (precision floor); benign at realistic parameters.
findings.remediationHint: Accrue phUSD at higher precision (scale before flooring) or document the minimum-rate threshold.

findings.title: REFUTED: collectReward permissionless re-anchor griefing + free claim() poke (V1 ledger M-02) is resolved in V2
findings.inheritedFrom: phlimbo-ea ledger M-02 (V1, refuted in V2)
findings.description: V1's griefing lever was the rewardPerSecond re-anchor inside _updatePool, exercisable for free via a non-staker claim() poke. V2 REMOVES that recompute from _updatePool (L465-467; rate now recomputed only in collectReward L309 and setDepletionDuration L208). A free claim()/stake()/withdraw() poke now only advances legitimate accrual (which every staker was owed anyway) and does NOT reset the depletion window, so there is no griefing payoff. collectReward additionally requires amount>0 (L299) and pulls real rewardToken via safeTransferFrom (L304), so it cannot be used as a free poke. LARGELY RESOLVED — no residual worth reporting.
findings.lawBasis: Documented for recall: confirms the V1 finding does not carry into V2.

findings.title: REFUTED: collectReward funding sandwich-MEV (V1 ledger L-07) is negligible in V2
findings.inheritedFrom: phlimbo-ea ledger L-07 (V1, refuted in V2)
findings.description: collectReward calls _updatePool BEFORE adding the new balance (L302), and the freshly added rewardBalance streams over depletionDuration rather than being credited instantly. A searcher who stakes immediately before a funding event only earns a pro-rata share of the stream over the full window (identical to any other staker) and cannot atomically extract the just-added rewards in the same block. The sandwich is negligible in V2.

findings.title: REFUTED: collectReward with totalStaked==0 does not leak funder value in V2
findings.inheritedFrom: phlimbo-ea ledger L-08 (V1, refuted in V2)
findings.description: When totalStaked==0, _updatePool early-returns after only bumping lastRewardTime (L447-450) WITHOUT decrementing rewardBalance. collectReward adds the full amount to rewardBalance and recomputes the rate (L306-309). No reward is 'distributed to nobody' — the funder's contribution is preserved in rewardBalance and becomes fully available to the first staker. No value leaks in V2.
findings.remediationHint: None (optional: skip the lastRewardTime bump so the empty-pool interval is not silently lost, but no value is at risk).

findings.title: Migrator role has full custody of all migrating users' deposits and rewards; a non-forwarding or buggy migrator strands user value
findings.description: By design (story-020), when the migrator calls stake/withdraw/claim on behalf of a user, withdrawn principal (L390-392) and all auto-claimed rewards (phUSD via L495, stable via L500, beneficiary=msg.sender) route to msg.sender — the migrator — not the user. For migrateDeposits this is intentional (the migrator funds the stake), but the routing means the migrator role is a full-custody intermediary for every migrating user: if the migrator (or a future contract granted the migrator role) ever calls withdraw/claim on a user, that user's funds and rewards land in the migrator. The current MigratorV1V2 only calls stake (never withdraw/claim) so it does not exercise the withdrawal-custody path, bounding the live exposure to the auto-claim-on-pre-existing-position case (ECON-002).
findings.economicImpact: Concentration of custody in the migrator role. With the audited MigratorV1V2 the practical leak is limited to ECON-002; the broader hazard is that any address the owner sets via setMigrator inherits withdraw/claim-to-self power over every user, so a buggy or non-forwarding migrator contract would strand user value.
findings.attackOrFootgun: footgun (the 'rewards/principal land in caller not user' routing is subtle and non-obvious; owner-set migrator role). Not a malicious-owner/migrator finding — flagged as the non-obvious custody consequence and a guardrail for future migrator wiring.
findings.lawBasis: Law 3 — non-obvious consequence of the migrator delegation routing; surfaced as an operational hazard with safe-wiring guidance, not as a malicious-actor vector.
findings.remediationHint: Restrict the migrator role to stake-only (reject migrator-delegated withdraw/claim), or route delegated withdraw/claim proceeds to `user` rather than msg.sender.

refutedSummary: ECON-012 (V1 M-02 collectReward re-anchor griefing) — RESOLVED in V2 (rate recompute removed from _updatePool; collectReward requires real transfer).
ECON-013 (V1 L-07 funding sandwich-MEV) — NEGLIGIBLE in V2 (_updatePool before balance add; streamed rewards).
ECON-014 (V1 L-08 zero-totalStaked leak) — NO LEAK in V2 (rewardBalance preserved).
EXCLUDED by mandate: Linear-depletion exponential-decay under-delivery (V1 M-04) — V2 removed the _updatePool rate recompute (verified L465-467).

accountingVerification.migratorPhUSDInvariant: phUSD.balanceOf(migrator) == totalPHUSD_deposited holds across arbitrary settle/migrate interleaving: settleDebt MINTS phUSD to users (does not touch migrator balance or totalPHUSD_deposited), migrateDeposits decrements both balance and totalPHUSD_deposited in lockstep via stake's safeTransferFrom. No desync between settle (which doesn't move the deposit float) and migrate. CONFIRMED CONSISTENT — the only failure mode is the strict-== donation/over-funding brick (ECON-001), not an accounting desync.
accountingVerification.migratorUSDCInvariant: usdc.balanceOf(migrator) == totalUSDC holds: settleDebt transfers usdcOwed[i] out and decrements totalUSDC in lockstep. CONFIRMED CONSISTENT.
